chordInfo.name: Minor Sixth Chords
chordInfo.subtitle: Discover the bittersweet sophistication of minor sixth chords - the tonic minor of jazz, essential for bossa nova and film noir harmony.

fundamentals.label: Definition
fundamentals.value: Four-note chords combining a minor triad with a major 6th

fundamentals.label: Function
fundamentals.value: Tonic minor in jazz, melodic minor harmony

applications.label: Jazz
applications.value: Tonic minor chord in jazz minor keys

boxes.title: Interval Quality
items: No 7th: Lighter and more resolved than m7

boxes.title: Scale Relationship
items: Key insight: Am6 = F#m7b5 in first inversion
Function: Stable minor tonic in jazz harmony

voicingGroups.title: Essential Minor Sixth Voicings
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These fundamental open-position minor sixth voicings are the easiest way to begin playing m6 chords on guitar.

voicings.name: Am6
voicings.fingering: Based on Am shape, add F# on 1st string (2nd fret)
voicings.use: Jazz tonic minor, bossa nova in A minor

voicings.name: Dm6
voicings.fingering: Based on Dm shape, add B on 1st string (open)
voicings.use: Jazz tonic minor, film noir harmony

voicings.name: Em6
voicings.fingering: Based on Em shape, add C# on 2nd string (2nd fret)
voicings.use: Jazz minor voicings, swing era comping

voicingGroups.title: Barre and Moveable Voicings
voicingGroups.tipDescription: These moveable shapes let you play minor sixth chords in any key across the fretboard.

voicings.name: Cm6 (barre)
voicings.fingering: 6th string root barre shape with added 6th
voicings.use: Any key using E-form barre, full voicing

voicings.name: Bm6
voicings.fingering: Based on Bm barre shape with added 6th

voicings.name: F#m6
voicings.fingering: Based on F#m7 shape, raise b7 to 6th
voicings.use: Jazz minor ii-V-i, bossa nova keys

items.title: Jazz Minor Tonic (im6-iv7-V7)
items.description: The minor sixth chord serves as a stable tonic in jazz minor keys, replacing the standard minor or minor seventh chord for a more refined, melodic minor sound.

items.title: Bossa Nova Pattern (im6-iim7b5-V7-im6)
items.description: Classic bossa nova progression where the minor sixth chord provides the warm, sophisticated tonic sound that defines the genre. Note the iim7b5 is the enharmonic equivalent of a m6 chord on a different root.

items.title: Film Noir Descent (im6-bVIMaj7-V7-im6)
items.description: The m6 chord's bittersweet quality perfectly captures the shadowy atmosphere of film noir soundtracks, descending through the flat sixth major seventh before resolving.

items.title: Swing Turnaround (im6-bVI7-iim7b5-V7)
items.description: Classic swing-era turnaround using the minor sixth as a departure point, cycling through related harmony back to the dominant for resolution. Common in big band arrangements.

techniqueItems: Practice the difference between m6 and m7 shapes on the same root
Focus on clean voicings and muting unused strings carefully
Use fingerpicking for bossa nova m6 comping patterns
Practice voice leading from m6 to its half-diminished equivalent
applicationItems: Use m6 as a jazz minor tonic instead of plain minor chords
Essential for authentic bossa nova and Brazilian jazz styles
Creates film noir atmosphere at slower tempos
Interchangeable with half-diminished chords for reharmonization

practiceExercises.title: Practice Exercises
practiceExercises.tipDescription: These exercises develop your ability to voice, hear, and apply minor sixth chords across musical contexts.

exercises.title: Exercise 1: Minor 6th vs Minor 7th Comparison
exercises.content: Pattern: Am6 - Am7 - Dm6 - Dm7 - Em6 - Em7
exercises.detail: Alternate between minor sixth and minor seventh on the same root to train your ear to the subtle but important difference in color
exercises.tip: The m6 sounds brighter and more resolved than the m7 - the raised 6th adds a melodic minor sweetness

exercises.title: Exercise 2: Bossa Nova Comping Pattern
exercises.content: Pattern: Am6 (2 bars) - Bm7b5 (1 bar) - E7 (1 bar)
exercises.detail: Practice a classic bossa nova syncopated rhythm using the ii-V-i in A minor with m6 as the tonic chord
exercises.tip: Keep the rhythm gentle and relaxed - bossa nova should feel effortless, with the thumb handling bass notes

exercises.title: Exercise 3: m6 and Half-Diminished Equivalents
exercises.content: Pattern: Am6 then F#m7b5, Dm6 then Bm7b5, Em6 then C#m7b5
exercises.detail: Play each minor sixth chord, then revoice the same four notes as its enharmonic half-diminished equivalent to hear the inversion relationship
exercises.tip: Same four notes, different bass note - understanding this unlocks advanced reharmonization and substitution possibilities

concepts.title: The m6 / Half-Diminished Relationship
items: Every m6 chord is a half-diminished chord in first inversion
Jazz players exploit this equivalence to find new voicings on familiar shapes
This relationship is the key to understanding melodic minor harmony

concepts.title: Minor Sixth in Melodic Minor Harmony
items: The m6 chord is the tonic (first degree) of melodic minor
Jazz minor = melodic minor ascending used in both directions
Contains both major 6th and major 7th over a minor triad
Foundation for altered dominants, lydian dominant, and superlocrian scales
